transcript.text: Samsung WW90T534DAW keeps coming up with 4C after a couple of minutes. Drum is dry. Any ideas before I call someone out?

The '4C' code on Samsung washing machines typically means the machine is not detecting enough water entering within the first few minutes of starting a cycle. This points to an issue getting water in rather than draining. 1. Check the tap: Ensure the isolation tap behind the machine (where the hose connects) is turned fully on.
2. Check for kinks: Make sure the fill hose isn't crushed or bent sharply against the wall.
3. Clean the inlet filter: Over time, grit or limescale can block the small mesh filter where the hose screws onto the back of the machine. This restricts flow so much that the machine thinks it's not filling at all. Could you please check if the tap is on and have a look inside that inlet mesh filter? Let me know what you find.
Tap was already open, I turned it fully anticlockwise anyway and no change. Hose isn't kinked. I'll unscrew the hose and check the filter now.

The 4C code suggests the machine isn't detecting enough water entering within the first few minutes. Since the tap was already open and the hose wasn't kinked, the most common cause is a blocked inlet mesh filter inside the machine's connection point. This small filter catches debris from your home's pipes; if it gets clogged with limescale or grit, water flow drops so low that the machine thinks there's no supply at all. Please let me know what you found when you checked that filter: was it blocked (and did cleaning it help), or was it already clean? If it was clean but the flow is still very weak, we'll need to check if your household water pressure itself has dropped.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the fill-hose mesh filter is" — A small mesh filter sits inside the fill-hose connector at the tap/valve end and catches grit. Turn the tap off, unscrew the hose and rinse the mesh. Typical layout — your machine may differ.]
Filter was clogged with grey grit and limescale bits. Cleaned it, put it back and it fills normally now, 4C has gone.

That’s excellent news. It sounds like the grit and limescale in that inlet filter were restricting the water flow just enough to trigger the 4C error. Since cleaning it has restored normal filling, you’ve sorted the issue yourself. To help prevent this from happening again, I’d suggest checking that inlet mesh once or twice a year (or if you notice the fill time getting longer) and giving it a quick rinse under the tap if any build-up appears. Is there anything else I can help you with regarding your washing machine?
